thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Customer Aurelia Health (single-tenant) SLO breach detected on /v1/chat/stream — p95 latency jumped from 210ms -> 2.3s, p99 -> 12.1s in the last 5m. Error rate steady. Streaming stalls observed. Autoscale attempted but tail queues growing.

sara: acked, I'm oncall. pulling traces + logs now. tagging @ryan for runtime signal.

ryan: on it. any recent deploys to that tenant's pool?

deploybot: Deploy event: customer/aurelia-health pool update by kevin at 1786721200. image: rw-runtime:v2026.03.12

maria: weird note from monitoring: unusual token mix — lots of unicode emoji ("🩺🔬💬") and zero-width joiners in prompts. KV cache hit ratio dropped ~40% for that tenant. Could be cache canonicalization mismatch.

sara: ok so two working hypotheses: 1) prompt pattern (emoji/unicode) causing cache misses -> increased per-token compute & longer KV lookups; 2) model kernel slowdown on long unicode tokens causing stalls.

kevin: i can roll back the pool image if needed but prefer a targeted mitigation first. can we route traffic off streaming to non-streaming fallback? that should reduce stall surface.

sara: agree. doing quick mitigation: set route fallback to non-streaming response mode for Aurelia. I'll also raise concurrency limit on their dedicated pool temporarily.

sara: runbook step: disable streaming for that route -> `rwctl routes update --customer aurelia-health --route /v1/chat --streaming disabled --reason "mitigate streaming stalls"`

maria: while that's running, grabbing a sample trace. trace id: `tr-1786723650-ae9f`. p99 spans show long kernel exec on `attention_kv_lookup` at ~8-11s. logs attached: ```
[1786723605] ctx=abc123 token="🩺" kv_lookup=0.003s
[1786723606] ctx=abc123 token="‍" kv_lookup=9.8s
[1786723607] ctx=abc123 model_exec=10.2s stall=1
```

ryan: that 9.8s kv_lookup screams unicode normalization edgecase. maybe our canonicalization logic treats ZWJ sequences badly and misses cache key. if cache miss -> full recompute of several layers.

lisa: customer support pinged Aurelia. they confirm a spike after a marketing campaign that included lots of emoji in user prompts. they reported degraded streaming UX around 17:00 UTC. no data exfil concerns.

kevin: rolling quick config change to add a normalization shim for that tenant to pre-normalize emoji sequences before tokenization. patch: `normalize_unicode = true` at route-level. doing canary to 2% of traffic.

sara: good. while canary running, I'm increasing dedicated pool soft concurrency from 48 -> 72 to soak existing backpressure. keep an eye on tail length.

deploybot: Route update applied (canary=2%). Pool concurrency updated for pool aurelia-dedicated-1 -> 72.

maria: canary results after 30s: 2% traffic normalized -> p95 for that slice down from 2.3s to 380ms, p99 down to ~1.1s. KV cache hit ratio for canary slice improved 63%.

sara: nice. expand normalization to 25% then 100% if stable. but we need permanent fix in runtime cache canonicalization. tagging @ryan for follow-up.

ryan: will do a patch to canonicalizer. early theory: ZWJ + variation selector sequences produced extremely long token substrings that bypassed our fast path. quick patch: normalize ZWJ sequences and cap key length. i'll open PR and run repro.

kevin: while that lands, suggestion: proactively create a model variant without streaming (non-streaming v1) and add a circuit-breaker to fallback if streaming takes >3s to first chunk. we can configure `fallback_timeout_ms=3000`.

sara: doing that now: `rwctl routes update --customer aurelia-health --route /v1/chat --fallback_model rw-gpt-medium-nostream --fallback_timeout_ms 3000`

maria: collecting artifacts for postmortem: traces, kv cache hit metrics, per-token latency histograms, and sample prompts (sanitized). also saving the canary experiment logs.

lisa: told Aurelia support that mitigation steps are active: normalization shim + concurrency bump + streaming fallback. Customer replied: "seeing improvements but some sessions still hit stalls" — they want ETA.

sara: ETA: normalization full rollout in 10m, concurrency bump stays, runtime canonicalizer PR by @ryan target EOD. full resolution depends on runtime patch; if PR delayed, keep the shim. I'll ask for eng-oncall handoff at 18:00 UTC for monitoring.

ryan: opened PR #3421 with tests and a repro script. will try to get patch reviewed ASAP. linking repro: https://git.internal/rw/runtime/issues/3421

kevin: quick perf note — even after normalization there is a small p99 delta vs baseline because of tokenization overhead; long-term we should improve tokenization path. filing tech-debt ticket.

sara: status update in 10m. current impact: p95 improved for normalized traffic; overall customer still above SLO at p99 (~3.2s) but trending down. assigning owners: mitigation=kevin, root-cause=ryan, customer-comms=lisa, postmortem=maria.

(10m later)

maria: full rollout of normalization completed at 1786723850. post-rollout p95=340ms, p99=720ms. streaming stalls dropped to near-zero. KV cache hit ratio recovered to baseline.

lisa: Aurelia support reports UX back to normal. they thanked the team. :tada:

sara: closing active incident. leaving follow-ups: 1) runtime canonicalizer PR to prod, 2) add emoji-heavy prompt testcases to evals, 3) improve tokenization benchmark for unicode joins, 4) add route-level circuit-breaker telemetry. will create postmortem doc and link here.

ryan: I'll merge PR after CI. assigning self to CR postmortem item.

incident-bot: Incident resolved — duration 27m. severity: P2. channel incident-summary posted to #incidents-archive.

sara: handoff to eng-oncall for overnight monitoring: @ryan pls pick up at 18:00 UTC. I'll update calendar. thanks all. :heart:
